body.x: Hurotics, a company founded by faculty members of the Chung-Ang University Assistive and Rehabilitation Robotics Lab and led by CEO Lee Gi-wook, participated in the 'CES Unveiled' global media event on January 7th, ahead of the official start of CES 2024 in Las Vegas.

Specializing in biomechanics and custom robotic suit technology, Hurotics has developed robot suits that apply to various walking disorders, showing high utility in medical, sports and leisure, industrial, and military markets.

Expanding its product portfolio into assistive wearable robots, which are in high demand but limited in development and supply, Hurotics sees this as an opportunity to explore global market entry. At CES Unveiled, the company showcased its 'H-Flex' series of walking assist robots, capturing the attention of attendees.

The H-Flex, an advanced soft robotic suit, features high-speed customized control, a compact embedded system, mechanical suit control software, and customized modular technology. Its all-in-one modular driving method fulfills all requirements for self-powered movement, allowing customization of the robotic assistance according to user conditions.

Utilizing H-Flex in the initial walking assist mode can improve walking efficiency by up to 20%. It also boasts excellent flexibility and adjustability to fit users' physical needs and reduces friction at body contact points with its unique dual-folding drive module.

body.cap: CEO Lee Gi-wook of Hurotics interacting with the international press at CES Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Furthermore, the user-customized software in H-Flex integrates a walking recognition algorithm and functions applicable to various users and environmental variables, personalizing assistance power and patterns within 2 minutes. The dedicated app allows users to track their current status, select preferred rehabilitation modes, and review activities to assess physical improvements.

CEO Lee Gi-wook stated, "We saw Unveiled as the most suitable and effective platform to showcase our products and technology, as it gathers various media and influencers from around the world ahead of CES 2024." He added, "Especially as our company is preparing for a Pre-A investment round, we expect that showcasing the technical capabilities and competitiveness of H-Flex to a broader international audience will aid in future investment attraction. We also aim to gauge the potential price point set just before commercialization through feedback from journalists."

The Consumer Technology Association (CTA), host of CES, the world's largest IT exhibition, provides a platform in Las Vegas each January to showcase global consumer electronics trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been reporting CES news worldwide since 2006, highlighting products, companies, and technologies with the 'BEST OF CES' and 'BEST OF MADE IN KOREA' awards programs. They also discuss issues in the field from the CES scene through 'AVING LIVE.'

The CES 2024 Seoul pavilion, operating on its most enormous scale since Seoul's first CES participation in 2020, is a joint effort of 13 organizations, including SBA, Seoul Bio Hub, Campus Town, AI Yangjae Hub, Gwanak District, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, Konkuk University, and Kyung Hee University. This collaborative pavilion marks a significant step in Seoul's ambition to become a startup hub, and among its participating companies, 17 received innovation awards, evidencing their excellence. The pavilion also includes 85 supporters in a significant collaboration between companies, institutions, and industry-academia cooperation.
